what_it_does: A single GPU is expensive, so cloud providers want to run multiple AI jobs on it at the same time — for example, a real-time inference service that must respond quickly alongside a slower model-training job running in the background. The trouble is that the jobs interfere with each other: the background job can slow down the time-sensitive service by nearly 3x, making shared GPUs impractical. Tally fixes this by acting as an invisible traffic controller between the two jobs. Rather than letting each job throw whole batches of work (called 'kernels', the programs that actually run on the GPU) onto the chip at once, Tally intercepts those launches and schedules them in smaller chunks — at the granularity of 'thread blocks', which are the small, self-contained groups of calculations that a GPU program is made of. By controlling how many thread blocks from each job run at any moment, Tally can protect the high-priority inference job from being starved. Crucially, applications do not need to be rewritten — Tally works as a shim layer that intercepts standard GPU calls.
